correctness.rationale: Starting with the exact source vector field, the alternating even-species ansatz gives C_N=(1-z²)/N, neighbor difference zero, and the scalar PDE z_t=D z_xx+(-a/N)z(1-z²). Anti-periodic sine symmetry supplies Dirichlet conditions on a half-circle; the energy identity and first Dirichlet eigenvalue give convergence at and below the exact cutoff, including equality. Above it, a positive subsolution excludes the zero equilibrium and the Jacobi-period identity proves uniqueness of the positive stationary Dirichlet profile. Compact gradient-flow omega limits imply convergence. Direct Lamé polynomial factorization yields a strictly positive periodic eigenfunction with the stated eigenvalue. All steps have explicit normalizations and parameter bounds; 22,610 finite exact/elementary checker assertions passed. Numerical PDE integrations were supplementary, not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The result addresses the source paper’s explicit motivated all-even frozen-wave conjecture, not an arbitrary parameter slice. It replaces a numerical extrapolation by a sharp if-and-only-if cutoff covering all even species sizes, proves nonconstant pattern selection where it survives, quantifies unavoidable periodic instability, and supplies a fully admissible N=52 counterexample where the proposed niches homogenize. The exact threshold separates ecologically interpretable finite-size regimes and rules out extrapolation from small cycles. A general downstream theorem is not required for this natural classification.
